question: Which of the following life processes leads to the breakdown of glucose in the absence of oxygen?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fermentation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fermentation is the breakdown of glucose into simpler products (such as ethanol and carbon dioxide, or lactic acid) in the absence of oxygen, i.e. it is a type of anaerobic respiration. (किण्वन — ऑक्सीजन की अनुपस्थिति में ग्लूकोज़ का विघटन)

 

• In yeast, glucose is broken down into ethanol (alcohol) + CO2, releasing a small amount of energy. This is the basis of the brewing and baking industries.

 

• In human muscle cells, during vigorous exercise when oxygen supply is insufficient, glucose is converted into lactic acid through anaerobic respiration, causing cramps and fatigue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aerobic respiration occurs in the presence of oxygen and breaks glucose down completely into CO2 and water, releasing much more energy (about 38 ATP) than anaerobic respiration (about 2 ATP).

 

• Louis Pasteur was the first to study fermentation scientifically, and it is widely used industrially to make curd, bread, wine and beer.

 

NOTE

 

• Aerobic respiration (Option A): Requires oxygen and takes place in the mitochondria; it is far more energy-efficient than fermentation.

 

• Excretion (Option B): The biological process of removing metabolic waste products from the body, unrelated to glucose breakdown.

 

• Digestion (Option D): The breakdown of complex food into simpler absorbable molecules, which happens before respiration, not the same process.

question: Which of the following eye defects is mainly due to the weakening of the power of accommodation with age?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Presbyopia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Presbyopia is an age-related eye defect caused by the gradual weakening of the ciliary muscles and loss of elasticity of the eye lens, which reduces the eye's power of accommodation. (जरा-दूरदृष्टि — आयु के साथ समंजन क्षमता का कमजोर होना)

 

• Because the lens can no longer become sufficiently convex, near objects cannot be focused clearly on the retina, so near vision is affected — this typically begins after the age of 40.

 

• Presbyopia is corrected using bifocal lenses, which have both concave (for distant vision, if needed) and convex (for near vision) portions in the same lens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Power of accommodation is the eye's ability to adjust its focal length by changing the curvature of the lens through the ciliary muscles, to focus on objects at different distances.

 

• The near point of a normal eye is about 25 cm, and the far point is at infinity.

 

• Common eye defects and their correction: Myopia — concave lens; Hypermetropia — convex lens; Astigmatism — cylindrical lens; Presbyopia — bifocal (convex) lens.

 

NOTE

 

• Astigmatism (Option A): Caused by an irregular (non-spherical) curvature of the cornea or lens, causing blurred vision at all distances; corrected with a cylindrical lens.

 

• Hypermetropia (Option B): Far-sightedness, where near objects appear blurred because the image forms behind the retina; corrected with a convex lens.

 

• Myopia (Option C): Near-sightedness, where distant objects appear blurred because the image forms in front of the retina; corrected with a concave lens.

question: Which of the following is a homogeneous mixture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Air.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Air is a homogeneous mixture of gases (mainly nitrogen and oxygen, with small amounts of carbon dioxide, argon and water vapour) because it has a uniform composition throughout and no visible boundaries between its components. (वायु — समांगी मिश्रण)

 

• In a homogeneous mixture, the components are so thoroughly mixed that a single phase is observed, and any sample taken from it has the same composition.

 

• A heterogeneous mixture, by contrast, has visibly distinct components or phases, such as oil floating over water, or sand grains mixed with iron filings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common homogeneous mixtures: salt solution, sugar solution, alloys (like brass, bronze), vinegar.

 

• Other common heterogeneous mixtures: soil, sand and water, a salad, smoke and fog (aerosols).

 

• A solution is always homogeneous, made of a solute dissolved in a solvent; a suspension and colloid are usually heterogeneous at the visible or microscopic level respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• Oil and water (Option A): Do not mix and form two separate, visible layers — a classic heterogeneous mixture.

 

• Soil (Option C): A heterogeneous mixture of minerals, organic matter, air and water, with visibly distinct particles.

 

• Sand and iron filings (Option D): Clearly two distinct, separable substances — a heterogeneous mixture that can be separated using a magnet.

question: Which of the following conditions will NOT increase the rate of evaporation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Decreased Wind Speed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Evaporation is the process by which a liquid changes into vapour at any temperature below its boiling point, and its rate depends on temperature, surface area, humidity and wind speed. (वाष्पीकरण की दर को प्रभावित करने वाले कारक)

 

• Decreasing the wind speed slows down the removal of water-vapour molecules from just above the liquid's surface, allowing the surrounding air to become saturated faster — this decreases, not increases, the rate of evaporation.

 

• Increasing wind speed, on the other hand, carries away the vapour molecules quickly, keeping the air around the liquid unsaturated and thereby increasing the rate of evaporation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rate of evaporation increases with: higher temperature, larger surface area, lower humidity and higher wind speed.

 

• Evaporation causes cooling because the particles that escape as vapour carry away energy (latent heat) from the remaining liquid, which is why sweating cools the human body.

 

• Evaporation is a surface phenomenon, unlike boiling, which occurs throughout the bulk of the liquid at a fixed temperature.

 

NOTE

 

• Decreased Humidity (Option A): Lower humidity means the air can hold more moisture, so it speeds up evaporation — not the answer.

 

• Increased Surface Area (Option B): A larger exposed surface allows more molecules to escape simultaneously, increasing evaporation — not the answer.

 

• Increased Temperature (Option D): Gives molecules more kinetic energy to escape into the vapour phase, increasing evaporation — not the answer.

question: What makes the brain suitable for thinking activities?
option_2: Its complex arrangement of many neurons
solution_text:
The correct answer is Its complex arrangement of many neurons.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The human brain is capable of thinking, reasoning, memory and decision-making because of its highly complex network of billions of interconnected neurons, particularly concentrated in the cerebrum. (मस्तिष्क — जटिल तंत्रिका कोशिका नेटवर्क)

 

• The cerebrum, especially its outer layer the cerebral cortex, is the seat of higher mental functions like thinking, learning, memory, and voluntary actions, and it is highly folded to accommodate a very large number of neurons in a small space.

 

• Neurons communicate with each other through synapses, forming vast interconnected circuits that allow complex information processing — this dense connectivity, not the brain's shape or location, is what enables thought.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The human brain has three main parts: forebrain (cerebrum, thalamus, hypothalamus), midbrain, and hindbrain (cerebellum, pons, medulla oblongata).

 

• The cerebellum controls balance and coordination of voluntary movements; the medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions like heartbeat, breathing and blood pressure.

 

• The brain and spinal cord together form the central nervous system (CNS), protected by the meninges and cerebrospinal fluid.

 

NOTE

 

• Its location near the ears (Option A): The brain's location in the skull is for protection, not the reason it can think.

 

• Its connection to the heart (Option C): The brain does receive blood from the heart for oxygen and nutrients, but this supply function is not what enables thinking.

 

• Its smooth surface (Option D): Incorrect — the brain's cortex is actually highly folded/convoluted (gyri and sulci) to increase surface area for more neurons, not smooth.

question: Which meristematic tissue has the highest levels of Auxin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Apical Meristematic tissue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Apical meristem, found at the tips of roots and shoots, has the highest concentration of the plant hormone auxin, which it produces and from where auxin is transported downward to control growth. (शीर्षस्थ विभज्योतक — सर्वाधिक ऑक्सिन)

 

• Auxin promotes cell elongation just behind the growing tip, and is responsible for phenomena such as apical dominance (suppression of lateral bud growth) and phototropism/geotropism (bending towards light/against gravity).

 

• Apical meristem is responsible for the plant's growth in length (primary growth), continuously adding new cells at the shoot and root tips.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing, undifferentiated cells with thin cell walls, dense cytoplasm and no vacuoles.

 

• Lateral meristem (e.g. vascular cambium, cork cambium) is responsible for growth in girth/thickness (secondary growth) of stems and roots.

 

• Intercalary meristem occurs at the base of leaves or internodes (common in grasses) and allows quick regrowth after grazing or cutting.

 

NOTE

 

• Intercalary Meristematic tissue (Option A): Located between mature tissues, mainly responsible for elongation of internodes/leaf bases, not the site of the highest auxin.

 

• Lateral Meristematic tissue (Option B): Responsible for increasing the girth of the stem/root, not associated with the highest auxin levels.

 

• Xylem (Option C): A permanent, differentiated conducting tissue (transports water/minerals), not a meristematic (dividing) tissue at all.

question: An object is said to be in uniform motion if:
option_1: it covers equal distances in unequal time intervals
option_2: it covers unequal distances in unequal time intervals
option_3: it covers unequal distances in equal time intervals
option_4: it covers equal distances in equal time intervals
solution_text:
The correct answer is it covers equal distances in equal time intervals.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An object is in uniform motion when it travels equal distances in equal intervals of time, no matter how small the time interval is — meaning its speed remains constant. (एकसमान गति — समान समय अंतराल में समान दूरी)

 

• In uniform motion, the speed (or velocity, if direction is also constant) does not change with time, so a graph of distance vs. time for uniform motion is a straight line.

 

• If the object covers unequal distances in equal time intervals, its speed is changing, and the motion is called non-uniform (accelerated) motion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Speed = distance ÷ time, and is a scalar quantity; velocity is the corresponding vector quantity (speed with direction).

 

• For uniform motion, the distance–time graph is a straight line through the origin (if starting from rest position) with constant slope; for non-uniform motion, it is a curve.

 

• Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity; uniform motion has zero acceleration.

 

NOTE

 

• Options A and C describe unequal distances or unequal time intervals, both of which represent non-uniform motion, not uniform motion.

 

• Option B (unequal distances in unequal time) does not by itself define any specific type of motion and does not describe uniform motion.

question: Which gas is used by animals to live under water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dissolved oxygen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aquatic animals such as fish use the oxygen dissolved in water for respiration, extracting it through specialised organs called gills. (जल में घुली ऑक्सीजन — जलीय जीवों की श्वसन)

 

• Atmospheric oxygen dissolves in water at the water's surface, and its solubility depends on temperature and pressure — colder water can hold more dissolved oxygen than warmer water.

 

• Fish gills have a rich network of blood capillaries with a large surface area, allowing efficient diffusion of dissolved oxygen from water into the blood, and carbon dioxide from the blood back into the water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aquatic mammals such as whales and dolphins breathe atmospheric oxygen through lungs and must surface periodically, unlike fish which use gills.

 

• Amphibians (like frogs) can respire through their moist skin (cutaneous respiration) in addition to lungs and gills at different life stages.

 

• Reduced dissolved oxygen in water bodies (due to pollution or eutrophication) can cause fish kills, as it becomes insufficient for respiration.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrogen (Option A): Present dissolved in water but not usable by most aquatic animals for respiration; it is metabolically inert for them.

 

• Carbon dioxide (Option B) and Dry carbon dioxide (Option C): CO2 is a waste product of respiration excreted by aquatic animals into water, not a gas they use to breathe; 'dry carbon dioxide' is not a meaningful respiratory gas.

question: In the following reaction, Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu, iron:
solution_text:
The correct answer is is oxidised.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In this displacement reaction, iron (Fe) displaces copper from copper sulphate solution: Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu. (लौह का ऑक्सीकरण — इलेक्ट्रॉन त्याग)

 

• Iron atoms lose electrons to form Fe²⁺ ions (going from oxidation state 0 to +2), which is the definition of oxidation (loss of electrons/increase in oxidation state).

 

• Simultaneously, copper ions (Cu²⁺) gain electrons to form solid copper metal (Cu), i.e. copper is reduced. This makes it a classic redox (oxidation-reduction) reaction, and specifically a displacement reaction since Fe is more reactive than Cu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• In any redox reaction, the substance that is oxidised (loses electrons) acts as the reducing agent, and the substance that is reduced (gains electrons) acts as the oxidising agent. Here Fe is the reducing agent and CuSO4 (Cu²⁺) is the oxidising agent.

 

• This reaction is visually demonstrated by dipping an iron nail in blue copper sulphate solution: the blue colour fades and a reddish-brown coating of copper deposits on the nail.

 

• The reactivity series places iron above copper, which is why iron can displace copper from its salt solution, but copper cannot displace iron.

 

NOTE

 

• is unchanged (Option A): Incorrect — iron's oxidation state changes from 0 to +2, so it is definitely chemically transformed.

 

• acts a catalyst (Option B): Incorrect — a catalyst is not consumed in a reaction, but here iron is consumed and converted into FeSO4.

 

• is reduced (Option D): Incorrect — it is copper (Cu²⁺ to Cu) that is reduced in this reaction, not iron.

question: In Spirogyra, each fragment develops into a complete individual. What can be the possible reason for this?
option_1: Fragmentation happens only under laboratory conditions.
option_3: Each cell is capable of independent growth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Each cell is capable of independent growth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Spirogyra is a simple, filamentous, multicellular green alga that reproduces asexually by fragmentation — the parent filament breaks into two or more pieces (fragments), each of which grows into a new filament. (स्पाइरोगायरा — विखंडन द्वारा प्रजनन)

 

• This is possible because each individual cell of Spirogyra is capable of independent growth and cell division, since the organism has a simple body structure without specialised, differentiated organs.

 

• As each cell divides mitotically and elongates, a small fragment grows lengthwise into a complete new filament identical to the parent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fragmentation is common in simple multicellular organisms with a simple body plan, such as Spirogyra and some fungi and algae; it occurs naturally in water bodies, not only under laboratory conditions.

 

• Other modes of asexual reproduction include binary fission (Amoeba, bacteria), budding (yeast, Hydra), spore formation (Rhizopus, ferns), and vegetative propagation (plants).

 

• Spirogyra can also reproduce sexually by conjugation, in which two filaments come close and exchange gametes through a conjugation tube to form a zygospore.

 

NOTE

 

• Fragmentation happens only under laboratory conditions (Option A): Incorrect — it is a natural process that occurs in ponds and slow-moving water bodies where Spirogyra grows.

 

• Each fragment has roots (Option B): Incorrect — Spirogyra is a simple filamentous alga and does not possess true roots, stems, or leaves.

 

• Each fragment has complex organs (Option D): Incorrect — Spirogyra has a very simple, undifferentiated body structure with no complex organs; that is exactly why simple fragmentation works.

question: Which of the following quantities represents the slope in a displacement–time graph?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Linear velocity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The slope of a displacement–time graph at any point gives the rate of change of displacement with time, which is by definition the velocity of the object. (विस्थापन-समय ग्राफ की प्रवणता — वेग)

 

• Mathematically, slope = (change in displacement) ÷ (change in time) = Δs/Δt = velocity, since displacement (a vector) is being considered, this slope specifically gives linear velocity (velocity along a straight line).

 

• A steeper slope indicates a higher velocity, a horizontal line (zero slope) indicates the object is at rest, and a negative slope indicates the object is moving back towards the starting point.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• On a velocity–time graph, the slope gives acceleration, and the area under the graph gives displacement.

 

• Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial to the final position (a vector), while distance is the total path length covered (a scalar).

 

• A curved displacement–time graph indicates non-uniform (accelerated) motion, since the slope (velocity) is continuously changing.

 

NOTE

 

• Acceleration (Option B): This is obtained from the slope of a velocity–time graph, not a displacement–time graph.

 

• Distance (Option C): This is the quantity plotted on the y-axis itself (or its scalar counterpart), not the slope of the graph.

 

• Speed (Option D): Speed is the scalar magnitude of velocity; the slope of a displacement-time graph gives velocity (which includes direction), more precisely termed here as linear velocity.

question: Plaster of Paris is prepared by heating which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gypsum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plaster of Paris (POP), chemically calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO4·½H2O), is prepared by heating gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) to about 373 K (100°C), which removes three-quarters of its water of crystallisation. (प्लास्टर ऑफ पेरिस — जिप्सम को गर्म करके)

 

• The reaction is: CaSO4·2H2O (gypsum) --heat--> CaSO4·½H2O (Plaster of Paris) + 1½H2O.

 

• When mixed with water, Plaster of Paris sets into a hard mass by re-absorbing water and reverting to gypsum, which is why it is used for making casts for fractured bones, moulds, toys and decorative items.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plaster of Paris must be stored in moisture-proof containers, as it can absorb atmospheric moisture and start to set/harden while in storage.

 

• Heating gypsum at a higher temperature (above 200°C) removes all water of crystallisation to form 'dead burnt plaster', which does not set with water and is not useful for construction purposes.

 

• Gypsum itself is also used directly as a fertiliser and in the manufacture of cement (to regulate its setting time).

 

NOTE

 

• Limestone (Option B): On strong heating (calcination) gives quick lime (CaO) and CO2, not Plaster of Paris.

 

• Slaked lime (Option C): Calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2, formed by adding water to quicklime; used in whitewashing, not related to Plaster of Paris.

 

• Baking soda (Option D): Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3), used in cooking and as an antacid; unrelated to Plaster of Paris production.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct about reproduction?

 

1. Bulls alone can produce a calf.

2. Hens alone can not produce new chicks.
option_1: Statement 2 is correct but Statement 1 is false.
option_4: Statement 1 is correct but Statement 2 is false.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Statement 2 is correct but Statement 1 is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is false: a bull alone cannot produce a calf, because a calf is produced by sexual reproduction, which requires the fusion of a male gamete (sperm, from the bull) with a female gamete (egg, from a cow). A bull alone can only provide sperm; it cannot give birth. (यौन प्रजनन — नर एवं मादा युग्मकों का संलयन आवश्यक)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: a hen alone (without fertilisation by a rooster/cock) cannot produce chicks, because although a hen can lay unfertilised eggs on its own, only a fertilised egg (formed after mating with a rooster) can develop into a chick.

 

• Reproduction in birds and mammals, including cattle and poultry, is a sexual process requiring both a male and a female parent to contribute genetic material.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• In sexual reproduction, offspring inherit genetic material from both parents, leading to genetic variation, unlike asexual reproduction where offspring are genetically identical (clones) to a single parent.

 

• Fertilisation is the fusion of the male gamete (sperm) and female gamete (egg/ovum) to form a zygote, which develops into a new individual.

 

• In cattle, gestation (pregnancy) typically lasts about 9 to 9.5 months, similar to humans.

 

NOTE

 

• Both statements are false (Option B): Incorrect, since Statement 2 is actually true (a hen alone cannot produce chicks without fertilisation).

 

• Both statements are correct (Option C): Incorrect, since Statement 1 is false (a bull, being male, cannot physically give birth to a calf).

 

• Statement 1 is correct but Statement 2 is false (Option D): Incorrect — this is the reverse of the actual truth values.

question: Which of the following tissues is very elastic and used to connect two bones in our body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ligament.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A ligament is a strong, elastic connective tissue that connects bone to bone at joints, allowing some flexibility of movement while holding the skeletal structure together. (स्नायु/लिगामेंट — हड्डी को हड्डी से जोड़ता है)

 

• Ligaments are composed mainly of elastin fibres (giving them elasticity) along with some collagen fibres, allowing them to stretch to a limited extent and then return to their original shape, which helps stabilise joints during movement.

 

• Ligaments are distinct from tendons, which connect muscle to bone and are relatively less elastic and more fibrous (mostly collagen), designed to transmit the force of muscle contraction to bones.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Connective tissue in the human body includes areolar tissue, adipose tissue, blood, bone, cartilage, ligaments, and tendons — all of which connect, support, or bind other tissues/organs together.

 

• Cartilage is a smooth, flexible connective tissue found at joints, in the nose, ear and between vertebral discs, reducing friction between bones.

 

• Common injuries related to ligaments include a sprain (overstretching or tearing of a ligament, often at the ankle or knee).

 

NOTE

 

• Macrophage (Option B): A type of white blood cell that engulfs pathogens and debris (phagocytosis); part of the immune system, not a connective structural tissue linking bones.

 

• Mast cell (Option C): An immune cell found in connective tissue that releases histamine during allergic/inflammatory responses; unrelated to joining bones.

 

• Adipocyte (Option D): A fat-storing cell found in adipose tissue, which provides insulation and energy storage, not bone connection.

question: The energy possessed by a moving object due to its motion is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is kinetic energy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion, given by the formula KE = ½mv², where m is the mass and v is the velocity of the object. (गतिज ऊर्जा — गति के कारण ऊर्जा)

 

• The faster an object moves, or the greater its mass, the more kinetic energy it possesses — since KE is proportional to the square of velocity, doubling the speed quadruples the kinetic energy.

 

• A moving car, a flowing river, and a falling stone all possess kinetic energy because of their motion; kinetic energy is zero when the object is at rest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration (e.g. an object held at a height has gravitational PE = mgh).

 

• The work-energy theorem states that the work done on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy.

 

• Mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy of an object, and in the absence of friction/air resistance, the total mechanical energy remains conserved (law of conservation of energy).

 

NOTE

 

• Chemical energy (Option A): Energy stored in the bonds of chemical compounds (e.g. in fuel or food), released during chemical reactions.

 

• Potential energy (Option B): Energy due to position or state, not motion — the opposite scenario to kinetic energy.

 

• Thermal energy (Option C): The internal energy of a substance due to the random motion of its constituent particles (molecules/atoms), not the directed motion of an entire object.

question: The effect of multiple reflections of sound in large halls or auditoriums is, ________.
option_2: it helps in uniform distribution of sound
solution_text:
The correct answer is it helps in uniform distribution of sound.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In large halls and auditoriums, sound waves undergo multiple reflections from the walls, ceiling and floor before reaching listeners, and when properly designed, this helps distribute sound uniformly throughout the hall so that people in all seats can hear clearly. (ध्वनि का बहु-परावर्तन — एकसमान वितरण में सहायक)

 

• This is why auditoriums often have specially curved or angled ceilings/walls to reflect sound waves evenly towards the audience rather than concentrating them in one area or letting them die out before reaching the back.

 

• However, if reflections are excessive or uncontrolled, they can cause reverberation (persistence of sound) that makes speech unclear, which is why sound-absorbing materials are also used in combination with reflecting surfaces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Reverberation is the persistence of sound due to repeated reflection; excessive reverberation is controlled using materials like carpets, curtains, perforated boards and cushioned seats that absorb sound.

 

• A concave/parabolic reflecting surface behind the stage (or a curved ceiling) is often used to direct sound waves towards the audience.

 

• The reflection of sound also has applications in megaphones, stethoscopes and SONAR.

 

NOTE

 

• it converts sound into heat (Option A): Some energy is lost as heat upon reflection/absorption, but this is not the primary or intended effect of multiple reflections in a hall.

 

• it eliminates all echoes (Option C): Incorrect — uncontrolled multiple reflections can actually cause unwanted echoes/reverberation rather than eliminate them.

 

• it blocks sound propagation (Option D): Incorrect — reflections help sound reach listeners in all parts of the hall; they do not block its propagation.

question: Which of the following is true about the magnetic field inside a solenoid?
option_3: It is uniform and in the form of parallel straight lines.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is uniform and in the form of parallel straight lines.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder; when current flows through it, it behaves like a bar magnet. (परिनालिका के अंदर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र — एकसमान एवं समांतर रेखाएँ)

 

• Inside a current-carrying solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform in magnitude and direction at every point, and the field lines run as parallel straight lines along the axis of the solenoid, similar to the field inside a bar magnet.

 

• This uniform field makes the solenoid extremely useful for creating a strong, consistent magnetic field, which is exploited in devices such as electromagnets, electric bells and MRI machines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Outside the solenoid, the magnetic field is similar in pattern to that of a bar magnet, being weak and non-uniform, emerging from one end (north pole) and entering the other (south pole).

 

• The strength of the magnetic field inside a solenoid can be increased by increasing the number of turns, the current, or by inserting a soft iron core (making it an electromagnet).

 

• The direction of the magnetic field due to current can be found by the right-hand thumb rule.

 

NOTE

 

• It forms random patterns (Option A): Incorrect — the field inside a solenoid is well-defined and orderly, not random.

 

• It is zero (Option B): Incorrect — this describes the field far outside a bar magnet or solenoid at large distances, but not the field inside the solenoid, which is strong and uniform.

 

• It is non-uniform (Option D): Incorrect — this describes the field outside the solenoid; inside, it is uniform.

question: An object has a weight of 24 N on Earth. What will be its weight on the Moon's surface?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4 N.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is about one-sixth (1/6) of that on the Earth, and since weight = mass × g, an object's weight on the Moon becomes one-sixth of its weight on Earth. (चंद्रमा पर भार — पृथ्वी के भार का 1/6)

 

• Given weight on Earth = 24 N, weight on Moon = 24 × (1/6) = 4 N.

 

• The object's mass remains the same everywhere (mass = 24/9.8 ≈ 2.45 kg on both Earth and Moon), but its weight changes because weight depends on the local value of gravitational acceleration, which is different on the Moon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mass is a scalar quantity measured in kilograms, representing the amount of matter in a body, and it does not change with location.

 

• Weight is a vector quantity, equal to the gravitational force on a body (W = mg), measured in newtons, and varies with the local value of g.

 

• The Moon's smaller gravity is due to its much smaller mass compared to Earth, in accordance with g = GM/R².

 

NOTE

 

• 240 N (Option A): Would result from multiplying, not dividing, by 10 — an incorrect approach; also 10× is not the correct ratio between Earth and Moon gravity.

 

• 144 N (Option B): Does not correspond to any standard Earth-Moon gravity ratio.

 

• 6 N (Option D): Would be the result of dividing 24 by 4 rather than by 6 — an arithmetic slip; the correct divisor is 6, giving 4 N.

question: Which of the following statements about the magnetic field due to a circular loop is true?
option_1: The field lines are parallel to the plane of the loop.
option_2: The field is uniform everywhere around the loop.
option_3: The field lines at the centre are circular.
option_4: The field depends on current and radius.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The field depends on current and radius.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The magnetic field produced at the centre of a current-carrying circular loop is given by B = μ₀I / (2r), where I is the current through the loop and r is its radius — so the field strength directly depends on both the current and the radius. (वृत्ताकार लूप के कारण चुंबकीय क्षेत्र — धारा एवं त्रिज्या पर निर्भर)

 

• As the current increases, the magnetic field at the centre increases; as the radius increases (for the same current), the field at the centre decreases, since B is inversely proportional to r.

 

• At the centre of the loop, the magnetic field lines are straight and perpendicular to the plane of the loop, not circular; the concentric circular field lines are found only around a straight current-carrying conductor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The direction of the magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop can be found using the right-hand thumb rule applied to the loop.

 

• If a coil has N turns, the field at the centre becomes B = μ₀NI / (2r), i.e. it increases proportionally with the number of turns.

 

• A solenoid (many circular loops stacked together) produces a strong, nearly uniform field inside it, unlike a single loop.

 

NOTE

 

• The field lines are parallel to the plane of the loop (Option A): Incorrect — at the centre, the field is perpendicular to the plane of the loop, not parallel to it.

 

• The field is uniform everywhere around the loop (Option B): Incorrect — the field varies with distance from the loop and is strongest at the centre, decreasing further away; it is not uniform everywhere.

 

• The field lines at the centre are circular (Option C): Incorrect — this describes the field around a straight wire; at the centre of a loop the field lines are straight (along the axis).

question: In a genetic lab, a fertilised human embryo is found to have XX chromosomes. Which of the following is true?
option_1: The embryo will become a human female.
option_2: The embryo has an extra Y chromosome.
option_3: The embryo will become a human male.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The embryo will become a human female.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In humans, sex is determined by the sex chromosomes: females have XX and males have XY. An embryo with XX chromosomes will develop into a human female. (XX गुणसूत्र — मादा भ्रूण)

 

• Every human egg (ovum) carries an X chromosome, while sperm can carry either an X or a Y chromosome. If a sperm carrying an X chromosome fertilises the egg, the resulting zygote is XX (female); if a sperm carrying a Y chromosome fertilises it, the resulting zygote is XY (male).

 

• This means the father's sperm determines the sex of the child, not the mother, since the mother always contributes an X chromosome.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Out of the 23 pairs of chromosomes in humans, 22 pairs are autosomes (non-sex chromosomes) and 1 pair is the sex chromosome (allosome).

 

• Sex determination in humans is called the XY type; other organisms use different systems, e.g. birds use the ZW type, where the female is ZW and the male is ZZ.

 

• Conditions like Klinefelter syndrome (XXY) and Turner syndrome (X0) arise due to abnormalities in the number of sex chromosomes.

 

NOTE

 

• The embryo has an extra Y chromosome (Option B): Incorrect — the embryo has XX, with no Y chromosome present at all.

 

• The embryo will become a human male (Option C): Incorrect — a male embryo would have XY, not XX.

 

• The embryo lacks sex chromosomes (Option D): Incorrect — the embryo does have sex chromosomes (a pair of X chromosomes); it is not devoid of them.

question: Which of the following is NOT a biotic loss during the storage of grains?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loss by inappropriate moisture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During grain storage, losses are classified as biotic (caused by living organisms) and abiotic (caused by non-living physical factors). Inappropriate moisture is an abiotic factor, since it is a physical/environmental condition, not a living organism. (अजैविक कारक — अनुपयुक्त नमी)

 

• Biotic factors causing storage loss include living pests such as insects, rodents (rats), mites, fungi and bacteria, which physically consume, contaminate, or spoil the stored grain.

 

• Abiotic factors causing storage loss include inappropriate moisture, inadequate/excessive temperature, and improper storage conditions, which affect grain quality without any living organism being directly involved.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Excess moisture in stored grain promotes the growth of fungi and bacteria, and encourages germination or rotting of grains.

 

• Common storage practices to reduce losses include drying grains properly before storage, using airtight containers, and applying preservatives such as dried neem leaves.

 

• India loses a significant percentage of its foodgrain production every year due to inadequate storage facilities, which is why schemes for building modern warehouses (like those under the Food Corporation of India) are important.

 

NOTE

 

• Loss by mites (Option A): Mites are tiny living arthropods that feed on stored grain — a biotic factor.

 

• Loss by rodents (Option B): Rats and mice are living organisms that eat and contaminate grain — a biotic factor.

 

• Loss by insects (Option D): Insects such as weevils and beetles are living pests that damage stored grain — a biotic factor.

question: Which of the following compounds is classified as a saturated hydrocarbon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) contain only single covalent bonds between carbon atoms, with the general formula CnH2n+2. Ethane (C2H6) has a single C–C bond and is therefore a saturated hydrocarbon. (संतृप्त हाइड्रोकार्बन — केवल एकल बंध)

 

• Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one double or triple bond between carbon atoms — alkenes (general formula CnH2n) have a double bond, and alkynes (general formula CnH2n-2) have a triple bond.

 

• Because it has only single bonds, ethane is relatively less reactive than alkenes/alkynes and undergoes substitution reactions rather than addition reactions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ethene (C2H4) is an alkene with one C=C double bond; it is used to artificially ripen fruits and is a starting material for polythene.

 

• Ethyne (C2H2), commonly called acetylene, is an alkyne with one C≡C triple bond; it is used in oxy-acetylene welding due to its high flame temperature.

 

• Benzene (C6H6) is an aromatic hydrocarbon with a ring structure containing alternating double bonds (a special kind of unsaturated compound), not a simple chain alkane.

 

NOTE

 

• Ethene (Option A): An unsaturated hydrocarbon (alkene) due to its C=C double bond.

 

• Ethyne (Option B): An unsaturated hydrocarbon (alkyne) due to its C≡C triple bond.

 

• Benzene (Option C): An unsaturated aromatic hydrocarbon with a cyclic ring of alternating double bonds, not saturated.

question:
The IUPAC name of following compound is ________.

CH3CHBrCH2CH2CH3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2-Bromopentane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The compound CH3–CHBr–CH2–CH2–CH3 has a chain of 5 carbon atoms (pentane) with a bromine atom attached at the 2nd carbon. (IUPAC नामकरण — कार्बन श्रृंखला की क्रमांकन)

 

• Numbering the carbon chain from the end that gives the substituent the lowest locant: C1(CH3)–C2(CHBr)–C3(CH2)–C4(CH2)–C5(CH3). The bromine is on carbon 2, so the compound is named 2-bromopentane.

 

• Since all bonds in the chain are single bonds (no double/triple bonds), the parent hydrocarbon is pentane (not pentene, which would require a C=C double bond).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• IUPAC nomenclature rules require selecting the longest continuous carbon chain as the parent chain, then numbering it to give the lowest possible locants to substituents/functional groups.

 

• A halogen substituent (like bromine) is named using the prefix 'bromo-', with its position indicated by a locant number before the parent hydrocarbon name.

 

• Compounds with the general formula CnH2n+1X (where X is a halogen) are called haloalkanes.

 

NOTE

 

• 2-Bromopentene (Option B): Incorrect — the compound has no double bond, so it cannot be named as a 'pentene'; the suffix '-ene' would require unsaturation.

 

• 3-Bromopentane (Option C): Incorrect locant — numbering from the correct end (giving the lowest locant) places bromine at position 2, not 3.

 

• 1-Bromopentane (Option D): Incorrect — this would mean bromine is on the terminal (first) carbon, but here it is on the second carbon of the chain.

question: During indigestion, the stomach produces too much acid, that may be neutralised by which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magnesium hydroxide (Milk of magnesia).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Milk of magnesia is the common name for a mild base, magnesium hydroxide [Mg(OH)2], which is used as an antacid to neutralise excess hydrochloric acid produced in the stomach during indigestion. (मिल्क ऑफ मैग्नीशिया — मैग्नीशियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड, प्रतिअम्ल)

 

• The neutralisation reaction is: Mg(OH)2 + 2HCl → MgCl2 + 2H2O, in which the base reacts with the acid to form a neutral salt and water, relieving the burning sensation and pain caused by excess acid.

 

• Antacids like magnesium hydroxide are chosen because they are mild bases, safe to consume, and effectively neutralise stomach acid without causing excessive alkalinity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common antacids include sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) and aluminium hydroxide.

 

• The stomach normally secretes hydrochloric acid (HCl), which helps in digestion of food and kills harmful bacteria; excess secretion causes indigestion, heartburn and acidity.

 

• A neutralisation reaction is the reaction between an acid and a base to form salt and water, with the general form: Acid + Base → Salt + Water.

 

NOTE

 

• Magnesium oxide (Option A): Also a base (MgO) but is not the compound actually known as 'Milk of Magnesia'; it is used as antacid in some formulations but is not the common name given here.

 

• Magnesium carbonate (Option B): Can act as an antacid too but is different from magnesium hydroxide, which is specifically what 'Milk of Magnesia' refers to.

 

• Magnesium sulphate (Option D): Known as Epsom salt, this is used as a laxative, not as an antacid for neutralising stomach acid.

question: When a ray of light passes through the optical centre of a spherical lens, it ________.
option_3: Gets deviated away from the normal
solution_text:
The correct answer is Emerges undeviated.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The optical centre of a spherical lens is the central point through which any ray of light passes without any deviation in its direction, emerging in a straight line from the point it entered. (प्रकाशिक केंद्र — बिना विचलन के गमन)

 

• This property is used as one of the standard rules for drawing ray diagrams for both convex and concave lenses: 'a ray passing through the optical centre goes straight through, without bending.'

 

• The optical centre lies at the geometric centre of the lens, on the principal axis, and this behaviour holds true for both convex (converging) and concave (diverging) lenses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The two other standard rules for ray diagrams in lenses are: (i) a ray parallel to the principal axis, after refraction, passes through (or appears to come from) the principal focus, and (ii) a ray passing through the principal focus, after refraction, becomes parallel to the principal axis.

 

• The focal length of a lens is the distance between the optical centre and the principal focus.

 

• Power of a lens = 1/focal length (in metres), measured in dioptres (D); convex lenses have positive power, concave lenses have negative power.

 

NOTE

 

• Bends toward the focus (Option A): This describes what happens to a ray parallel to the principal axis (for a convex lens), not a ray through the optical centre.

 

• Gets deviated away from the normal (Option C): Incorrect — a ray through the optical centre does not deviate at all; this describes ordinary refraction behaviour elsewhere on the lens.

 

• Always reflects back (Option D): Incorrect — a lens works by refraction (bending/transmitting light), not reflection; light passing through the optical centre is transmitted, not reflected.

question: Simplify: [(3x)³ − (4z)³] ÷ [9x² + 12xz + 16z²] × (3x + 4z)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 9x² − 16z².

 

GIVEN

 

• [(3x)³ − (4z)³] ÷ [9x² + 12xz + 16z²] × (3x + 4z)

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the identity a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²), with a = 3x and b = 4z.

 

• a² = 9x², ab = 12xz, b² = 16z², so a² + ab + b² = 9x² + 12xz + 16z² — exactly the denominator given.

 

• (3x)³ − (4z)³ = (3x − 4z)(9x² + 12xz + 16z²).

 

• Dividing by (9x² + 12xz + 16z²) cancels that factor, leaving (3x − 4z).

 

• Multiplying by (3x + 4z): (3x − 4z)(3x + 4z) = (3x)² − (4z)² = 9x² − 16z².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever you see a³ − b³ over (a² + ab + b²), instantly cancel to get (a − b) — no need to expand the cubes at all.

 

NOTE

 

• Key identities to memorise: a³ − b³ = (a−b)(a²+ab+b²); a³ + b³ = (a+b)(a²−ab+b²); (a−b)(a+b) = a² − b².

question: A person saves 60% of his income. If his expenditure is ₹600, then his income (in ₹) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹1,500.

 

GIVEN

 

• Savings = 60% of income, so Expenditure = 40% of income = ₹600.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let income = ₹100 (assumed). Expenditure = 100 − 60 = 40 parts, corresponding to ₹600.

 

• 40% of income = 600 ⇒ Income = 600 × 100/40 = ₹1,500.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Income = Expenditure ÷ (Expenditure %) × 100 = 600 ÷ 40 × 100 = 1,500.

 

NOTE

 

• Always express 'saves x%' as 'spends (100 − x)%' before applying the percentage-to-value formula.

question: Navya and Bhavya can paint a house in 50 days and 75 days, respectively. If they work on alternate days, starting with Bhavya, in how many days can the duo complete painting that house?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 60 days.

 

GIVEN

 

• Navya alone: 50 days; Bhavya alone: 75 days; they work on alternate days, starting with Bhavya.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take total work = LCM(50, 75) = 150 units. Navya's rate = 150/50 = 3 units/day; Bhavya's rate = 150/75 = 2 units/day.

 

• Work done in each pair of days (Bhavya's day + Navya's day) = 2 + 3 = 5 units.

 

• Number of such 2-day pairs needed for 150 units = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 pairs = 60 days.

 

• Checking: after exactly 30 pairs (60 days, ending on Navya's day), total work = 30 × 5 = 150 units = the whole tank — the work finishes exactly at the end of day 60, with no partial day left over.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine work per 2-day cycle (Bhavya's rate + Navya's rate) and divide total work by this cycle sum; if it divides evenly, that many cycles (×2 days) is the exact answer.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check whether the total finishes exactly at the end of a full cycle or partway through the next slower/faster worker's turn — here it worked out to an exact whole number of cycles.

question: A cylindrical pipe, open at both ends, has an external diameter of 20 cm and an internal diameter of 16 cm. If the length of the pipe is 35 cm, find the volume of the metal used in making the pipe. (Use π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 3960 cm³.

 

GIVEN

 

• External diameter = 20 cm ⇒ R = 10 cm; internal diameter = 16 cm ⇒ r = 8 cm; length h = 35 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume of metal (a hollow cylinder) = π(R² − r²)h.

 

• R² − r² = 100 − 64 = 36.

 

• Volume = (22/7) × 36 × 35 = 22 × 36 × 5 = 3960 cm³.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• R² − r² = (R−r)(R+r) = (10−8)(10+8) = 2 × 18 = 36 — quicker than squaring both separately.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Open at both ends' just tells you it's a hollow tube (no extra end-caps to add/subtract) — use π(R²−r²)h directly for the metal volume.

question: The cost of a washing machine is 25% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 34% and that of the TV decreases by 21%, then what is the percentage change in the total cost of 4 washing machines and 2 TVs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Increase by 12%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Washing machine (WM) cost is 25% less than TV cost. WM cost increases by 34%; TV cost decreases by 21%. Quantities: 4 WMs and 2 TVs.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let TV cost = ₹100, so WM cost = 100 − 25% of 100 = ₹75.

 

• New WM cost = 75 × 1.34 = ₹100.50; new TV cost = 100 × 0.79 = ₹79.

 

• Original total (4 WM + 2 TV) = 4×75 + 2×100 = 300 + 200 = ₹500.

 

• New total = 4×100.50 + 2×79 = 402 + 158 = ₹560.

 

• % change = (560 − 500)/500 × 100 = 60/500 × 100 = 12% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Assume a convenient base value (TV = 100) to instantly get WM = 75 from '25% less', then just track rupee totals before/after — avoids fraction-heavy percentage-on-percentage algebra.

 

NOTE

 

• 'x% less than TV' means WM = TV × (1 − x/100); don't confuse it with 'TV is x% more than WM', which gives a different base.

question: Simplify: [2½ ÷ 5/8 + 3/4 × 2/3 − 5/6] ÷ [(15 − 6)² ÷ 9 + 1/2]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 22/57.

 

GIVEN

 

• [2½ ÷ 5/8 + 3/4 × 2/3 − 5/6] ÷ [(15 − 6)² ÷ 9 + 1/2]

 

SOLUTION

 

• Numerator: 2½ = 5/2. 5/2 ÷ 5/8 = 5/2 × 8/5 = 4.

 

• 3/4 × 2/3 = 1/2.

 

• Numerator = 4 + 1/2 − 5/6 = (24 + 3 − 5)/6 = 22/6 = 11/3.

 

• Denominator: (15 − 6)² = 9² = 81. 81 ÷ 9 = 9. 9 + 1/2 = 19/2.

 

• Value = (11/3) ÷ (19/2) = 11/3 × 2/19 = 22/57.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Simplify numerator and denominator completely and separately first (as two clean fractions), then divide — avoids handling one giant nested fraction at once.

 

NOTE

 

• Always resolve mixed numbers (like 2½ → 5/2) into improper fractions before doing division/multiplication with other fractions.

question: A person's income and expenditure are in the ratio 9 : 5. His income rises by 60% while his expenditure falls by 10%. If his initial expenditure was ₹15,500, then what will be his final saving (in ₹)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹30,690.

 

GIVEN

 

• Income : Expenditure = 9 : 5. Initial expenditure = ₹15,500. Income rises by 60%, expenditure falls by 10%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Expenditure = 5 parts = ₹15,500 ⇒ 1 part = ₹3,100.

 

• Income = 9 parts = 9 × 3,100 = ₹27,900.

 

• New income = 27,900 × 1.60 = ₹44,640.

 

• New expenditure = 15,500 × 0.90 = ₹13,950.

 

• Final saving = New income − New expenditure = 44,640 − 13,950 = ₹30,690.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use the given ratio directly to find '1 part' from the known expenditure value, then scale income off that same part value — faster than working with percentages of an unknown income.

 

NOTE

 

• Saving = Income − Expenditure, always computed using the NEW (changed) values when the question asks for the final saving.

question: A sum of money is to be distributed among A, B, C and D in the ratio 6 : 7 : 17 : 19. If C gets ₹250 more than B, then how much did A receive?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹150.

 

GIVEN

 

• A : B : C : D = 6 : 7 : 17 : 19. C's share exceeds B's share by ₹250.

 

SOLUTION

 

• C − B (in ratio parts) = 17 − 7 = 10 parts = ₹250.

 

• So 1 part = 250 ÷ 10 = ₹25.

 

• A's share = 6 parts = 6 × 25 = ₹150.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Find the value of '1 part' using the two ratio terms whose rupee difference is directly given, then simply scale up A's ratio number.

 

NOTE

 

• Always subtract ratio terms (not shares) first to isolate '1 part', especially when a rupee difference (not a total) is given.

question: The length of the shadow of a vertical tower is equal to its height. Find the angle of elevation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 45°.

 

GIVEN

 

• Shadow length = Height of the tower.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let height = shadow = h. tan(angle of elevation) = height/shadow = h/h = 1.

 

• tan θ = 1 ⇒ θ = 45°.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever shadow = height, the angle of elevation is always 45° (since tan 45° = 1) — memorise this instantly-recognisable case.

 

NOTE

 

• Standard tan values to remember: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

question: A train passes two tunnels of length 2091 m and 1259 m in 89 seconds and 63 seconds, respectively. What is the length of the train?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 757 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Tunnel 1 = 2091 m, crossed in 89 s. Tunnel 2 = 1259 m, crossed in 63 s. Same train speed both times.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let train length = L m and speed = v m/s. To 'pass' a tunnel, the train covers (tunnel length + L).

 

• v = (L + 2091)/89 = (L + 1259)/63.

 

• Cross-multiplying: 63(L + 2091) = 89(L + 1259).

 

• 63L + 131733 = 89L + 112051.

 

• 131733 − 112051 = 89L − 63L ⇒ 19682 = 26L.

 

• L = 19682 ÷ 26 = 757 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up (L + d1)/t1 = (L + d2)/t2 directly from 'same speed' and cross-multiply — this is the standard approach whenever two tunnel/platform crossings share one train speed.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Crossing a tunnel/platform' always means distance = (length of train + length of tunnel/platform), not just the tunnel length alone.

question: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 4 : 3. Six years later, the ratio will be 5 : 4. Find the difference between their present ages.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 6 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• Present ages: P : Q = 4 : 3. Six years later, P : Q = 5 : 4.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let present ages be P = 4x, Q = 3x.

 

• Six years later: (4x + 6)/(3x + 6) = 5/4.

 

• Cross-multiply: 4(4x + 6) = 5(3x + 6) ⇒ 16x + 24 = 15x + 30 ⇒ x = 6.

 

• P = 4×6 = 24 years, Q = 3×6 = 18 years.

 

• Difference = 24 − 18 = 6 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The difference in ages never changes with time, so you could also solve using x from the ratio alone: difference = (4x − 3x) = x = 6 years, once x is found.

 

NOTE

 

• Always add the SAME number of years to both people's ages when handling 'x years later/ago' ratio problems.

question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 65, 41, 96, 44, 38, 30, 79, 90 and 21 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 56.

 

GIVEN

 

• Observations: 65, 41, 96, 44, 38, 30, 79, 90, 21 (9 values).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum = 65+41+96+44+38+30+79+90+21.

 

• Adding step by step: 65+41=106; +96=202; +44=246; +38=284; +30=314; +79=393; +90=483; +21=504.

 

• Mean = 504 ÷ 9 = 56.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Pair numbers that sum to round figures while adding (e.g. 41+59-style pairing) to reduce arithmetic slips; here just add carefully in a single left-to-right pass and divide by the count (9).

 

NOTE

 

• Mean = (sum of all observations) ÷ (number of observations) — always double-check the count of terms before dividing.

question: The number of prime numbers lying between 480 and 489 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• Numbers strictly between 480 and 489, i.e. 481 to 488.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 481 = 13 × 37 (not prime). 482, 484, 486, 488 are even (not prime, except 2).

 

• 483 = 3 × 161 (not prime). 485 = 5 × 97 (not prime).

 

• 487: check divisibility by primes up to √487 ≈ 22.1, i.e. 2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19 — none divide it exactly (487 is odd, digit sum 19 not divisible by 3, doesn't end in 0/5, and 487÷7, ÷11, ÷13, ÷17, ÷19 all leave remainders). So 487 is prime.

 

• Only one prime number (487) lies in this range.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• To test primality quickly, only check divisibility by primes up to √n (here √487 ≈ 22, so just 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19 need checking).

 

NOTE

 

• Eliminate all even numbers and multiples of 5 first — that quickly narrows a 9-number range down to just a couple of candidates to test.

question: A car travels for 180 km at a speed of 60 km/hr and then returns along the same route at a speed of 45 km/hr. By how many minutes is the return journey longer than the onward journey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 60 min.

 

GIVEN

 

• Distance = 180 km each way. Onward speed = 60 km/hr; return speed = 45 km/hr.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Onward time = 180/60 = 3 hours = 180 minutes.

 

• Return time = 180/45 = 4 hours = 240 minutes.

 

• Difference = 240 − 180 = 60 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Time = Distance/Speed; since 180 is a common multiple of both 60 and 45, the times come out as whole hours (3 h and 4 h), making the minute conversion trivial.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert to the same time unit (minutes here) before subtracting, since the question specifically asks for the difference in minutes.

question: A class of 91 students took a Physics test. 12 students had an average score of 64. The other students had an average score of 77. What is the average score (rounded up to one decimal place) of the whole class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 75.3.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total students = 91. 12 students: average = 64. Remaining (91 − 12 = 79) students: average = 77.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total marks of first group = 12 × 64 = 768.

 

• Total marks of second group = 79 × 77 = 6,083.

 

• Total marks of whole class = 768 + 6,083 = 6,851.

 

• Average of whole class = 6,851 ÷ 91 = 75.285... ≈ 75.3 (rounded to one decimal place).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combined average = (n1×a1 + n2×a2) / (n1+n2); compute the two group totals separately and add before dividing by the combined count — never average the two given averages directly since the group sizes differ.

 

NOTE

 

• The printed options in the source appear as 'A).7, B).6, C).4, D).3' — read alongside the computed value 75.3, this matches option D, whose visible digits are '.3'.

question: One pipe can fill a tank in 4 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 8 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• Filling pipe: fills the tank in 4 minutes. Emptying pipe: empties a full tank in 8 minutes. Both opened together, tank starts empty.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Filling rate = 1/4 tank per minute. Emptying rate = 1/8 tank per minute.

 

• Net filling rate (both open) = 1/4 − 1/8 = 2/8 − 1/8 = 1/8 tank per minute.

 

• Time to fill 1/4 of the tank = (1/4) ÷ (1/8) = 1/4 × 8 = 2 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net rate = (fill rate) − (empty rate); once you have the net rate, time for ANY fraction of the tank = (required fraction) ÷ (net rate).

 

NOTE

 

• Always subtract the emptying pipe's rate — students often mistakenly add both rates when pipes work in opposite directions.

question: Two-fifth of Vijay's marks in Hindi are more than one-third of his marks in Sanskrit by 5, while five times his marks in Hindi and five times his marks in Sanskrit together are equal to 310. Find his marks in Sanskrit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 27.

 

GIVEN

 

• Let Hindi marks = H, Sanskrit marks = S. (2/5)H = (1/3)S + 5. Also 5H + 5S = 310.

 

SOLUTION

 

• From 5H + 5S = 310: H + S = 62 ⇒ H = 62 − S.

 

• From (2/5)H − (1/3)S = 5, multiply throughout by 15: 6H − 5S = 75.

 

• Substitute H = 62 − S: 6(62 − S) − 5S = 75 ⇒ 372 − 6S − 5S = 75 ⇒ 372 − 11S = 75.

 

• 11S = 372 − 75 = 297 ⇒ S = 297 ÷ 11 = 27.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert both conditions into simple linear equations (clear fractions by multiplying by the LCM) and solve by substitution — this avoids working with fractions throughout.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double check: H = 62 − 27 = 35; verify (2/5)(35) = 14 and (1/3)(27) + 5 = 9 + 5 = 14 ✓.

question: The sides of a triangle are 148 cm, 57 cm, and 175 cm. What is the length (in cm) of its altitude corresponding to the side with a length of 57 cm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 140.

 

GIVEN

 

• Triangle sides: a = 148 cm, b = 57 cm, c = 175 cm. Need altitude on the side of length 57 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Semi-perimeter s = (148 + 57 + 175)/2 = 380/2 = 190.

 

• By Heron's formula, Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] = √[190 × (190−148) × (190−57) × (190−175)] = √[190 × 42 × 133 × 15].

 

• 190 × 42 = 7,980; 133 × 15 = 1,995; 7,980 × 1,995 = 15,920,100.

 

• √15,920,100 = 3,990 (since 3990² = 15,920,100), so Area = 3,990 cm².

 

• Altitude on side 57 cm: h = (2 × Area) ÷ base = (2 × 3,990) ÷ 57 = 7,980 ÷ 57 = 140 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a scalene triangle with all three sides given, Heron's formula is the fastest route to the area, from which any altitude follows via h = 2×Area/base.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check the square root carefully: 3990² = 3990×3990 = 15,920,100, confirming the area computation is exact (a clean number is a good sign the arithmetic is right).

question: In a triangle XYZ, ∠X − ∠Y = 40° and ∠Y − ∠Z = 25°. The ratio of ∠Z to ∠X − ∠Y is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 3 : 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• ∠X − ∠Y = 40°, ∠Y − ∠Z = 25°, and ∠X + ∠Y + ∠Z = 180° (angle sum property of a triangle).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let ∠Z = z. Then ∠Y = z + 25, and ∠X = ∠Y + 40 = z + 65.

 

• Sum: (z + 65) + (z + 25) + z = 180 ⇒ 3z + 90 = 180 ⇒ 3z = 90 ⇒ z = 30°.

 

• So ∠Z = 30°, and ∠X − ∠Y = 40° (given directly).

 

• Required ratio = ∠Z : (∠X − ∠Y) = 30 : 40 = 3 : 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Express all three angles in terms of a single variable (the smallest angle here) using the given differences, then apply the 180° angle-sum rule directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Since ∠X − ∠Y = 40° is given directly in the question, there is no need to recompute it after solving for the angles — just use it as-is in the final ratio.

question: What is the difference between the simple interest on a principal of ₹3,600 being calculated at 15% per annum for 3 years and 14% per annum for 4 years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. ₹396.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal = ₹3,600. Case 1: rate = 15% p.a., time = 3 years. Case 2: rate = 14% p.a., time = 4 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• SI = (P × R × T)/100.

 

• SI₁ = (3600 × 15 × 3)/100 = ₹1,620.

 

• SI₂ = (3600 × 14 × 4)/100 = ₹2,016.

 

• Difference = 2,016 − 1,620 = ₹396.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Compute each SI using P×R×T/100 separately when the R×T products differ (15×3=45 vs 14×4=56) — a common single formula shortcut doesn't apply since R and T both differ.

 

NOTE

 

• Simple interest is always directly proportional to R×T; here R×T = 45 for case 1 and 56 for case 2, so case 2 gives more interest despite the lower rate, because of the longer time.

question: Simplify: 2.3̅4̅ − 1.8̅9̅
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 4/9.

 

GIVEN

 

• 2.3̅4̅ means 2.343434... (the block '34' repeats forever); 1.8̅9̅ means 1.898989... (the block '89' repeats forever).

 

SOLUTION

 

• 2.343434... − 1.898989... : subtract directly using the repeating decimal expansions.

 

• (2 − 1) + (0.343434... − 0.898989...) = 1 + (−0.555555...) = 1 − 0.5555... = 0.4444...

 

• 0.4444... = 4/9 (a standard pure recurring decimal: 0.d̅ = d/9).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For pure recurring decimals x.a̅b̅, convert to a fraction using x + (ab)/99 (e.g. 2.34̅ = 2 + 34/99 = 232/99, and 1.89̅ = 1 + 89/99 = 188/99); then (232 − 188)/99 = 44/99 = 4/9 in lowest terms.

 

NOTE

 

• A bar over a 2-digit block means that whole block repeats — don't mistake it for a bar over only the last digit; always convert to p/q form (using the '/99' rule for a 2-digit repeating block) to avoid decimal subtraction errors.

question: After selling 88 phones, a store owner incurred a loss which is equal to the selling price of 8 phones. Find his loss percentage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 8⅓%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Selling 88 phones results in a loss equal to the selling price (SP) of 8 phones.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let SP of 1 phone = p. Total SP (of 88 phones) = 88p.

 

• Loss = SP of 8 phones = 8p.

 

• Since Loss = Cost Price (CP) − SP, CP = SP + Loss = 88p + 8p = 96p.

 

• Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (8p ÷ 96p) × 100 = 800/96 = 8⅓%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever loss (or profit) equals the SP of 'n' articles out of 'N' sold, Loss% = n/(N+n) × 100 (or Profit% = n/(N−n) × 100 for a profit case) — here 8/(88+8) × 100 = 8/96 × 100 = 8⅓%.

 

NOTE

 

• Never divide the loss by SP by mistake — loss/profit percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price, not the Selling Price.

question: If A : B = 4 : 6 and B : C = 7 : 12, then A : B : C is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 14 : 21 : 36.

 

GIVEN

 

• A : B = 4 : 6 (= 2 : 3 in lowest terms). B : C = 7 : 12.

 

SOLUTION

 

• To combine, make the B-terms equal: A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 7 : 12.

 

• LCM of the B-terms (3 and 7) = 21.

 

• A : B = 2 : 3 → multiply by 7 → 14 : 21.

 

• B : C = 7 : 12 → multiply by 3 → 21 : 36.

 

• Combined: A : B : C = 14 : 21 : 36.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• To merge two ratios sharing a common term, always scale both ratios so the shared term (B here) becomes the LCM of its two given values.

 

NOTE

 

• Simplify each given ratio to lowest terms first (4:6 → 2:3) before finding the LCM — it keeps the numbers smaller and the arithmetic cleaner.

question: Sachin got a new curtain at 12% discount. If Sachin did not get any discount, Sachin would have to pay ₹747 extra. So how much did Sachin pay for the curtain?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. ₹5,478.

 

GIVEN

 

• Discount = 12% on marked price (MP). Extra amount payable without discount = ₹747.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The 'extra ₹747' is exactly the discount amount, i.e. 12% of MP = ₹747.

 

• MP = 747 ÷ 0.12 = ₹6,225.

 

• Amount actually paid = MP − Discount = MP × (1 − 0.12) = 6,225 × 0.88 = ₹5,478.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Find MP first from the given discount amount (Discount% of MP = ₹747), then compute paid amount as 88% of MP directly, rather than working backwards from the paid amount.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Extra amount without discount' always equals the discount amount itself — this is the key insight that turns the word problem into a simple percentage equation.

question: A vendor offers her customers a discount of 29% on her beauty products and she still makes a profit of 12%. What is the cost price (in ₹) of a beauty product marked at ₹896?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 568.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked Price (MP) = ₹896. Discount = 29%. Profit after discount = 12%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − 0.29) = 896 × 0.71 = ₹636.16.

 

• Since profit = 12% on Cost Price (CP): SP = CP × 1.12.

 

• CP = SP ÷ 1.12 = 636.16 ÷ 1.12 = ₹568.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Chain the two percentage operations: CP = MP × (1 − discount%) ÷ (1 + profit%) = 896 × 0.71 ÷ 1.12 = 568, all in one line.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute SP from MP first (applying the discount), and only then relate SP to CP using the profit percentage — do not apply the profit percentage to the MP directly.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

9 12 10 13 11 ? 12
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 14.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 9, 12, 10, 13, 11, ?, 12

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the pattern of changes: 9→12 (+3), 12→10 (−2), 10→13 (+3), 13→11 (−2), 11→? (+3), ?→12 (−2).

 

• The series alternates +3, −2, +3, −2, +3, −2 ...

 

• 11 + 3 = 14. (Check: 14 − 2 = 12, which matches the last given term.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For alternating series, write out the differences between consecutive terms first — an alternating +/− pattern jumps out immediately.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the missing term using the term AFTER it too (not just the one before), to confirm the alternating pattern holds both ways.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

19 36 53 70 87 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 104.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 19, 36, 53, 70, 87, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Differences: 36−19=17, 53−36=17, 70−53=17, 87−70=17 — a constant difference of 17 (arithmetic progression).

 

• Next term = 87 + 17 = 104.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a simple arithmetic series, just check the first two differences — if they match, the whole series has a fixed common difference; add it once more to get the answer.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse a constant-difference (AP) series with one having a growing/shrinking difference — always check at least two consecutive gaps before assuming the pattern.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the letter-cluster pair that DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. KP-MJ.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pairs: OT-QM, MR-OK, QV-SO, KP-MJ (compare each pair's own internal letter-position gaps).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the alphabet-position gap within the FIRST letter-pair of each cluster, and separately within the SECOND letter-pair.

 

• OT: O(15)→T(20) = +5. MR: M(13)→R(18) = +5. QV: Q(17)→V(22) = +5. KP: K(11)→P(16) = +5. (All match, +5.)

 

• QM: Q(17)→M(13) = −4. OK: O(15)→K(11) = −4. SO: S(19)→O(15) = −4. MJ: M(13)→J(10) = −3 (breaks the pattern!).

 

• OT-QM, MR-OK and QV-SO all follow (+5, −4); only KP-MJ follows (+5, −3), making it the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert every letter to its alphabet-position number (A=1...Z=26) and compute the gap for BOTH halves of each cluster pair — the odd cluster will break the pattern in one of the two gaps.

 

NOTE

 

• Since the note excludes consonant/vowel-count-based logic, always default to checking numeric alphabet-position differences first for these letter-cluster puzzles.

question: Each of the digits in the number 5236789 is arranged in ascending order from left to right. The position(s) of how many digits will remain unchanged as compared to that in the original number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Four.

 

GIVEN

 

• Original number: 5 2 3 6 7 8 9 (positions 1 to 7).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Arrange digits in ascending order: 2 3 5 6 7 8 9.

 

• Compare position by position: Pos1: 5 vs 2 (different). Pos2: 2 vs 3 (different). Pos3: 3 vs 5 (different). Pos4: 6 vs 6 (same). Pos5: 7 vs 7 (same). Pos6: 8 vs 8 (same). Pos7: 9 vs 9 (same).

 

• Digits unchanged in position: 6, 7, 8, 9 — that's 4 digits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Write the original and the sorted number one below the other, position by position, and simply count the matching columns — this is faster and less error-prone than tracking each digit's movement individually.

 

NOTE

 

• Since 6, 7, 8, 9 already appear in increasing order at the tail of the original number, they naturally stay fixed after sorting; only the disordered leading digits (5, 2, 3) shift.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order?

TGA, UID, VKG, WMJ, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. XOM.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: TGA, UID, VKG, WMJ, ? — analyse each of the three letter-positions separately.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letters: T(20), U(21), V(22), W(23) → +1 each time → next = X(24).

 

• 2nd letters: G(7), I(9), K(11), M(13) → +2 each time → next = O(15).

 

• 3rd letters: A(1), D(4), G(7), J(10) → +3 each time → next = M(13).

 

• Combining: X O M = XOM.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 3-letter clusters, always split into 3 separate single-letter columns and find each column's own constant step (+1, +2, +3 here) — the columns are almost always independent simple APs.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check by re-verifying at least two consecutive gaps per column before finalising, since a single-gap check can occasionally be a coincidence.

question: Gautam starts from Point Y and drives 34 km towards the east. He then takes a right turn, drives 68 km, turns right and drives 55 km. He then takes a right turn, drives 11 km. He takes a right turn, drives 81 km. He then turns left, drives 57 km and stops at Point Z. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point Y again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 60 km towards the west.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at Y, facing east. Moves: 34 km east → right → 68 km → right → 55 km → right → 11 km → right → 81 km → left → 57 km, stop at Z.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take Y as origin (0,0); East = +x, North = +y. Start facing East, move 34 east: (34, 0).

 

• Right turn (East→South), move 68 south: (34, −68).

 

• Right turn (South→West), move 55 west: (34−55, −68) = (−21, −68).

 

• Right turn (West→North), move 11 north: (−21, −68+11) = (−21, −57).

 

• Right turn (North→East), move 81 east: (−21+81, −57) = (60, −57).

 

• Left turn (East→North), move 57 north: (60, −57+57) = (60, 0) = Point Z.

 

• Y is at (0,0); Z is at (60,0). To return from Z to Y, move 60 units in the −x direction, i.e. 60 km towards the west.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the net East-West (x) and North-South (y) displacement using a coordinate system — most of the intermediate north/south movements here cancel out (68 south vs 11+57=68 north), leaving a clean pure east-west answer.

 

NOTE

 

• Direction to 'return' is always opposite to the net displacement direction of the final point from the start — here Z is 60 km east of Y, so the return path is 60 km west.

question:
Refer to the given number series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

(Left) 6 8 5 2 4 9 1 6 3 2 7 1 6 9 3 8 5 4 2 1 7 8 6 5 9 7 2 (Right)

How many such even numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an even number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 6 8 5 2 4 9 1 6 3 2 7 1 6 9 3 8 5 4 2 1 7 8 6 5 9 7 2 (27 numbers, positions 1 to 27).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan for the pattern (odd number) — (even number) — (even number), and mark the middle even number each time it occurs.

 

• Position 4: sequence is 5(odd), 2(even), 4(even) → 2 qualifies (preceded by odd 5, followed by even 4).

 

• Position 18: sequence is 5(odd), 4(even), 2(even) → 4 qualifies (preceded by odd 5, followed by even 2).

 

• Position 22: sequence is 7(odd), 8(even), 6(even) → 8 qualifies (preceded by odd 7, followed by even 6).

 

• No other even number in the series has both an odd number immediately before it and an even number immediately after it.

 

• Total qualifying even numbers = 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mark every number as O (odd) or E (even) first in one pass, then simply scan for the literal 3-letter pattern 'O-E-E' in that O/E string — much faster than repeatedly checking actual values.

 

NOTE

 

• Always count from left to right as instructed, and remember the first and last numbers of the series can never qualify (they lack either a 'preceding' or a 'following' neighbour).

question:
In a certain code language,

'A ? B' means 'A is the daughter of B'

'A = B' means 'A is the son of B'

'A @ B' means 'A is the father of B'

'A √ B' means 'A is the sister of B'

Based on the above, how is C related to L if 'C @ D = E √ F ? L'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Daughter's husband.

 

GIVEN

 

• Codes: ? = daughter of, = = son of, @ = father of, √ = sister of. Expression: C @ D = E √ F ? L.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'C @ D': C is the father of D.

 

• 'D = E': D is the son of E, so E is a parent of D (here, since C is already the father, E must be D's mother, i.e. C and E are a couple).

 

• 'E √ F': E is the sister of F, so F is E's sibling — meaning F and E share the same parent(s), and L (below) is that parent.

 

• 'F ? L': F is the daughter of L, so L is a parent of F (and therefore also of E, since E and F are siblings) — so L is E's father (or mother).

 

• Putting it together: L is the parent of E; E is C's wife (co-parent of D with C). So C is married to L's daughter (E), which makes C the husband of L's daughter, i.e. C is L's daughter's husband.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Decode the chain one symbol at a time from left to right, writing a simple family-tree sentence for each link, then work out the overall relationship at the end — trying to solve it all in one step usually leads to errors.

 

NOTE

 

• In blood-relation puzzles with custom symbols, always keep a scratch note of 'who is whose parent/child/sibling' as you decode each symbol — it prevents losing track of the generations involved.

question:
A, B, C, D, W, X and Y are sitting in a straight line, facing the north.

Only three people sit to the left of D. Only A sits to the right of C. Only three people sit between C and B. X sits at some place to the left of Y but at some place to the right of W.

How many people sit between W and Y?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN
